name: Tretinoin for scalp

lead: Tretinoin is an approved acne and anti-aging retinoid. Hair-loss users mix it into minoxidil, or apply it to the scalp, hoping for better minoxidil absorption and more regrowth and density.
The proposed idea is that tretinoin helps minoxidil convert to its active sulfate form and penetrate the scalp. Reference sources describe the evidence for this use as weak and contradictory.

paras: It is used off-label, typically combined with a minoxidil solution applied to thinning areas as part of a daily routine. Users generally expect months before judging results.
Irritation, peeling and sun sensitivity are common; oral forms carry pregnancy warnings. One case report describes scalp infection with a combination lotion.

angle.text: Users mix tretinoin into minoxidil, believing it improves absorption and gives fuller regrowth and denser-looking hair. It is an approved acne retinoid used off-label here, working through the proposed step of better minoxidil activation and penetration. Reference sources describe the evidence for the hair use as weak and contradictory.

lead: Tretinoin (all-trans retinoic acid) is a topical retinoid approved for acne and widely studied for photoaging.[1] In hair-loss communities it is sometimes applied to the scalp or mixed with minoxidil on the theory that it improves minoxidil absorption.
Wikipedia describes the proposed idea as tretinoin helping minoxidil convert to its active sulfate form and penetrate the scalp, and characterises the evidence as weak and contradictory.[1]

paras: Tretinoin has been explored as an adjunct for hair loss, mainly in combination with minoxidil.[1]
In skin, tretinoin binds retinoic acid receptors in keratinocytes and normalises follicle keratinisation.[1] The proposed hair mechanism involves enhancing minoxidil sulfation and penetration.[1]

Topical use commonly causes irritation, redness, swelling, peeling and sun sensitivity; oral tretinoin is contraindicated in pregnancy.[1] A case report describes kerion celsi, a fungal scalp infection, in a woman using a tretinoin, minoxidil and betamethasone valerate lotion.[2]
No studies found for tretinoin scalp use in androgenetic alopecia in the sources used here, beyond the case report above.[2]

lore.intro: Tretinoin is discussed as a minoxidil booster.

claims.claim: Adding tretinoin to minoxidil boosts absorption and results.
